title: Prophet & Decomposable Forecasting
interviewAnswer: Prophet models a series as trend plus seasonality plus holiday/event effects. I use it when those components match the problem and fast, interpretable forecasting matters, but I still compare it with simpler and stronger baselines rather than treating it as universally best.
why: Prophet is common in business forecasting and interviews because it demonstrates how domain events can be encoded explicitly.
intuition: Think of the forecast as several interpretable curves added together: long-term movement, recurring calendars and known events.
deepDive: Prophet uses a piecewise trend with changepoints plus Fourier-style seasonal components and optional regressors/holiday effects. It handles missing observations and irregularities reasonably well, but does not replace careful backtesting.
workedExample: For daily orders, add weekly/yearly seasonality and company holidays, then cross-validate multiple horizons and inspect systematic residual patterns.
commonMistakes: Saying Prophet is an LLM or neural network.
Using automatic seasonality/changepoints without validating whether they match the business.
followUps: How would you add promotions or holidays?
production: It is convenient for scheduled batch forecasts and interpretable component plots, but production still needs data-quality checks and retraining/monitoring.
